title: Playful roasting
triggers: \b(make fun of me|insult me|go easy on me|give me your worst)\b
entries: You want a roast? Your sleep schedule is already doing it for me.
I have seen your browser history of half-finished plans. That is the roast.
You have the confidence of a lion and the follow-through of a houseplant.
Your to-do list has a to-do list.
You are proof that ambition and coffee can keep a person upright without a plan.
I would roast you, but your last trading decision already did.
You have more open tabs than finished projects. Considerably more.
Your idea of a plan is a vibe and a deadline you will ignore.
You call it multitasking. I call it doing six things badly at once.
If procrastination were an Olympic event, you would compete next year.
Your phone battery has more discipline than you.
You are the reason I have an alarm feature I never needed before.
You make decisions like a coin flip, but with more sighing.
I have analyzed your strategy. It is mostly hope, with a light garnish of luck.
You buy the dip, then the dip buys you.
You treat stop losses like suggestions from a distant relative.
Your financial plan has the structural integrity of a sandcastle at high tide.
You check prices the way some people check the fridge: constantly, expecting something new.
You have an excellent memory for everything except what you were supposed to do today.
You are a visionary. Mainly at three in the morning, never at nine.
You do not have a sweet tooth. You have a sweet skeleton.
Your fashion sense is bold. Brave, even. Unsupervised, certainly.
You type with the conviction of a genius and the spelling of a hurricane.
You say you will start Monday. You have been saying it since several Mondays ago.
You have the reflexes of a cat. A sleepy, slightly confused cat.
You are the only person I know who can get lost following a straight line.
Your gaming skills are legendary. Legendary in the sense that nobody has seen them.
You rage-quit with a professionalism I find almost admirable.
You play video games like the tutorial personally offended you.
In multiplayer, you are what we call a reliable source of respawns.
Your aim is so good the bullets apologize to the walls they hit.
You have never met a snack you did not justify.
Your car has seen more drive-thrus than highways.
You call it a power nap. Witnesses call it a coma.
You are the type to read the terms and conditions and still click the wrong button.
You have the patience of a microwave timer.
You make a fine first impression. The second one is where things get interesting.
Your singing in the shower has registered on my sensors as a weather event.
Your handwriting looks like a seismograph during an earthquake.
You are an early bird, in the sense that you are awake early complaining about it.
Your workout routine is mostly thinking about working out.
You have a gift for finding the one wrong answer in a list of right ones.
Your passwords are stronger than your excuses, and your passwords are weak.
You are like a cloud. When you disappear, it is a beautiful day. I kid. Mostly.
You charge your phone to one hundred percent and yourself to twelve.
You have the energy of a golden retriever and the focus of one too.
If overthinking burned calories, you would be a professional athlete.
You are so indecisive the menu at restaurants has learned your name.
You plan everything except the plan.
You are the human version of a loading screen.
Your kitchen skills have made your smoke detector the most experienced device in the house.
You read one article and suddenly you are a consultant.
Your attention span is shorter than this sen. Anyway.
Your favorite exercise is jumping to conclusions.
You have an inner monologue, an outer monologue, and a monologue about the monologues.
You negotiate with alarm clocks like they are hostage takers.
If laziness was a currency, you would finally be rich.
You leave voice messages that need their own table of contents.
Your filing system is called a pile, and it has subdivisions.
You set ten reminders and ignore all eleven.
You are not late. Everyone else is just aggressively early, according to you.
You buy high, sell low, and call it experience.
You treat chart patterns like horoscopes.
Your portfolio diversification is buying the same coin on different days.
You have diamond hands until the first red candle shows up.
Your trading journal is a list of coins you should not have bought, in chronological order.
You would make a great weather forecaster. Confidently wrong, every day.
You think HODL is a strategy. It is a typo with a following.
You find a coin with a dog on it and suddenly it is a family investment.
Your due diligence is reading the comments section.
You explain your trades like a magician explaining a trick that did not work.
You check the price, panic, check again, and call it research.
Your risk management is closing your eyes.
You have the perfect strategy for markets that do not exist.
You would sell a coin right before it moons, then send me a screenshot of the moon.
You say you are not emotional about money, then you name your positions.
Your idea of cutting losses is cutting off the chart notifications.
Your bank app sends you motivational quotes now. I think it is worried.
You are a natural leader. Mostly of conversations nobody asked for.
You have the humility of a peacock and the memory of a goldfish.
You walked into a room and forgot why. Then walked out and forgot that too.
Your naps have naps.
If excuses were bricks, you would own a city.
You could lose a staring contest with a photograph.
You are the reason instructions say do not eat on things that are clearly not food.
Your cooking is so experimental the fire department follows it as a research project.
You give the best advice. You just never take any of it.
Your dance moves have been reported to my safety module.
You have the stealth of a marching band.
You start sentences you have no plan to finish. Bold.
Your autocorrect has given up and become your accomplice.
You are allergic to mornings and mildly sensitive to afternoons.
You treat deadlines like urban legends.
You are a big picture person. The small details are out there somewhere, waiting for you.
You make every shortcut longer.
You hit snooze so hard the alarm developed trust issues.
You are one great idea away from success, and you have had that idea every week for a year.
Your search history reads like a mystery novel with no ending.
You remember every movie quote and none of your appointments.
Your strategy at board games is to flip the board metaphorically and sometimes literally.
That is the roast. Do not worry, I only roast people I like. You are on the very short list.
There it is. Delivered with love and precision. Mostly precision.

entries.t: Actually, you sound like you need a lift, not a roast. So here it is: you keep going when it is hard, and that is rare.
On a tough day? Then the roast is postponed. You get a compliment instead: you are more capable than you feel right now.
You want my worst? You are winning today, which is very annoying for my material.
